subject: SIG questionnaire delivery + KMS/ISO clarifications
messages:
From: Mike Hart <mike.hart@greenlinefinancial.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@greenlinefinancial.com
Date: 2027-04-01T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: SIG questionnaire and evidence mapping request

Marcus —

Thanks for taking this on. Greenline is working through an enterprise procurement review and the security team asked us to get a complete SIG questionnaire (v2.1) with a control map and sampled evidence for the controls that are in-scope for our SaaS use (data processing, KMS, key rotation, multi-tenant isolation, incident response).

Can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood can provide a control crosswalk from SIG to SOC 2 / ISO 27001 for the controls you consider in-scope.
- A list of representative evidence artifacts we can expect (reports, logs, architecture diagrams).
- KMS specifics: where keys are stored (customer-managed KMS vs Redwood-managed), rotation cadence, and whether you can produce rotation logs for audit periods.

Our timeline is tight — procurement would like the materials by EOD Friday (2027-04-02). If you need an extension please let me know and we can negotiate a narrow window.

Thanks,
Mike
Mike Hart
Security Procurement Lead
Greenline Financial


From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mike Hart <mike.hart@greenlinefinancial.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-01T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire and evidence mapping request

Mike —

Appreciate the clear ask. Quick confirmation and plan:

1) Crosswalk: we will deliver a SIG->SOC 2/ISO 27001 control crosswalk (matrix) that flags the authoritative evidence for each control and whether it is satisfied by Redwood platform controls, customer configuration, or third-party attestations.

2) Representative artifacts: we'll supply a short packet that includes:
   - Redacted SOC 2 Type II report (recent period)
   - Control mapping spreadsheet (SIG->SOC2/ISO)
   - KMS key rotation log extracts and a short statement of key management options (Redwood-managed vs customer-managed)
   - Architecture diagram showing tenant isolation boundaries and dataflow
   - Incident response runbook excerpt (for the controls requested)

3) KMS specifics: by default hosted customers use Redwood-managed keys in a region-specific KMS with HSM-backed providers (we also support customer-managed CMKs using AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault in our Private offering). Rotation cadence for Redwood-managed keys is 90 days; we can produce rotation logs for the requested audit window (subject to redaction for secrets).

We can get an initial package to you by EOD tomorrow (2027-04-02). Neha (CC) will attach the mapping and the SOC 2 redacted report; Priya will follow up with KMS log downloads and the architecture diagram.

If Greenline needs any custom extracts (e.g., key IDs for a specific tenancy or region), let us know the account identifiers and we'll scope that separately (may require a formal PO/data request).

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Manager, Assurance & Security
Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-04-02T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: SIG control map and artifacts (Greenline)

Mike —

Attaching the initial deliverables per Marcus' plan. Contents:

- redwood_sig_control_map_v2.xlsx (SIG->SOC2/ISO mapping; column notes indicate evidence owner and redaction guidance)
- redwood_soc2_type2_2026_redacted.pdf (redacted TSP and customer-specific data omitted)
- kms_key_rotation_logs_2026Q4.pdf (log extracts; key IDs partially masked)

Attachment notes / highlights:
- KMS: the attached log extract shows rotation events and the HSM provenance header for Redwood-managed keys. For a full unredacted pull we require a signed data request and an NDA addendum (standard for customer-specific key IDs).
- Tenant isolation: the mapping points to our runtime isolation controls (namespaces, per-tenant kernels) and the architecture diagram link included below.
- Evidence scope: the mapping flags which artifacts are global (platform controls), which are account-specific, and which are third-party (e.g., cloud provider attestations).

Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cRedwood-Greenline-RFI (architecture diagram + runbook excerpts). HubSpot record HS-43217 is updated with attachments.

If you want a short walkthrough (15–20 min) tomorrow morning to go through the control map line-by-line, I can set that up.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_sig_control_map_v2.xlsx, redwood_soc2_type2_2026_redacted.pdf, kms_key_rotation_logs_2026Q4.pdf

From: Mike Hart <mike.hart@greenlinefinancial.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG control map and artifacts (Greenline)

Thanks — we got the package and I appreciate the clear mapping. A couple quick follow-ups before procurement signs off:

1) For the KMS logs: can you confirm whether the rotation events include the key material provenance (i.e., HSM serial/event IDs) in the production logs or only in the redacted extracts? We may need the unredacted provenance for our internal audit; please advise the process/timeline and if a PO is required.

2) For ISO 27001: does Redwood maintain a current ISO 27001 certificate? If so, can you provide the cert or the scope statement (we'd like to reconcile any overlap with SIG controls).

If those two items are available early next week, procurement can finalize the paperwork. If we need to schedule a walkthrough, Thursday morning (04/08) would work for our team.

Regards,
Mike
Security Procurement Lead
Greenline Financial
